events.title: Launch of Sputnik 1
events.description: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial Earth satellite, from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. The metal sphere orbited Earth for about three months, transmitting radio beeps that were heard around the world.
events.significance: It marked the start of the Space Age and the Space Race between the United States and the Soviet Union, prompting major investments in science education and the creation of NASA in 1958.

events.title: Adoption of the Gregorian Calendar Begins
events.description: In Catholic countries including Italy, Spain, Portugal, and Poland-Lithuania, October 4, 1582 was followed directly by October 15, as the Gregorian calendar replaced the Julian calendar under Pope Gregory XIII's reform.
events.significance: The reform corrected accumulated drift in the calendar's alignment with the solar year and evolved into the civil calendar used by most of the world today.

events.title: Death of Francis of Assisi
events.description: Francis of Assisi, the Italian friar and founder of the Franciscan Order, died near Assisi on the evening of October 3, with his feast day observed on October 4. He was canonized in 1228 by Pope Gregory IX.
events.significance: His emphasis on poverty, humility, and love of nature reshaped medieval Christian spirituality, and he is the patron saint of animals and ecology; his feast day is World Animal Day.

events.title: Belgium Declares Independence
events.description: The provisional government of Belgium declared the country independent from the United Netherlands following the Belgian Revolution that began in August 1830.
events.significance: It led to the establishment of the Kingdom of Belgium as a neutral, constitutional monarchy, recognized by the major European powers in 1831.

events.title: Mount Rushmore Carving Begins
events.description: Sculptor Gutzon Borglum began carving the monument in the Black Hills of South Dakota, depicting Presidents George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, and Abraham Lincoln.
events.significance: Completed in 1941, Mount Rushmore became one of the most recognizable American national memorials and a major tourist destination.
